questions.title: Bubble Sort Mechanism
questions.description: Bubble sort works by repeatedly:
questions.Option1: selecting the minimum and moving it to the front
questions.Option2: comparing adjacent pairs and swapping them when out of order
questions.Option3: inserting each element into a sorted prefix
questions.Option4: splitting the array into halves and merging

questions.title: Selection Sort Mechanism
questions.description: In each pass, selection sort:
questions.Option1: bubbles the largest element to the end by adjacent swaps
questions.Option2: shifts each new element back into a sorted prefix
questions.Option4: finds the minimum of the unsorted part and swaps it into the front position

questions.title: Insertion Sort Mechanism
questions.description: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix by:
questions.Option1: taking the next element (key) and shifting larger elements right to insert it
questions.Option2: swapping distant elements chosen by a stride
questions.Option3: finding the minimum and swapping it forward
questions.Option4: recursively sorting halves and merging them

questions.title: Nearly-Sorted Favourite
questions.description: Which basic sort performs best on an ALREADY nearly sorted array?
questions.Option1: selection sort — it always scans the whole unsorted part
questions.Option2: bubble sort without a swapped flag — always n^2 comparisons
questions.Option3: insertion sort — few shifts, near O(n)
questions.Option4: merge sort — it needs an extra array

questions.title: Already-Sorted Swaps
questions.description: Bubble sort with a swapped flag runs on an already sorted array. How many swaps happen?
questions.Option2: 0 — the first pass makes no swap and the sort stops

questions.title: Selection Sort Invariant
questions.description: After pass k of selection sort (k = 1, 2, ...), the first k positions contain:
questions.Option1: the k largest elements, in sorted order
questions.Option2: k elements in their final positions only if the array was random
questions.Option3: the k smallest elements, in sorted order
questions.Option4: whatever elements were swapped during that pass, unsorted

questions.title: Worst Case Trio
questions.description: The WORST-case time complexity of bubble, selection and insertion sort is:
questions.Option2: O(n log n) for all three
questions.Option4: O(n) for bubble, O(n^2) for the others

questions.title: Stable Basic Sort
questions.description: Which of these basic sorts is STABLE (equal keys keep their original relative order)?
questions.Option2: none of the three basic sorts
questions.Option4: selection sort and bubble sort both

questions.title: Why Stability Matters
questions.description: Stability of a sort becomes important when:
questions.Option1: records with equal keys must keep their original order (e.g. sort students by marks, keeping roll order)
questions.Option3: memory must be minimised at all costs
questions.Option4: the data is always already sorted

questions.title: Best Case O(n) Sorts
questions.description: Which sorts achieve O(n) BEST-case time on an already sorted array?
questions.Option2: bubble sort (with a swapped flag) and insertion sort
questions.Option4: none — the best case of all three is O(n^2)

questions.title: Fewest Swaps on Reverse Input
questions.description: On a reverse-sorted array of n elements, which basic sort performs the FEWEST swaps (ignoring shifts and comparisons)?
questions.Option1: bubble sort — it makes about n(n-1)/2 swaps
questions.Option2: selection sort — at most n-1 swaps
questions.Option3: insertion sort — it swaps for every out-of-place element
questions.Option4: they all perform exactly n(n-1)/2 swaps
